answer: The cheapest real defence: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because summit only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, canyon is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
